title: The family-generated algebraically trivial Picard subgroup
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Write $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ for the group of isomorphism classes of invertible modules with tensor product as addition [def-sc-picard-group, def-sc-invertible-module]. Define $\operatorname{Pic}^{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ as the subgroup generated by $[L_{s_1}]-[L_{s_0}]$, where $S$ is a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $s_0,s_1\in S(k)$, and $L$ is invertible on $X\times_kS$. The family pairs, products, and their tensor-pullback fibres are precisely the generating pairs in [def-sfb-line-algebraic-equivalence]: adding isomorphic pairs contributes only zero and does not change this subgroup. Equivalently, take the subgroup generated by the differences of the two Picard classes whose representatives form one such generating pair.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, printed pp.12-13: the auxiliary affine-product Picard argument. This is the explicit family-generated subgroup specified in lem-sfb-affine-product-algebraic-equivalence, not a claim that Guo explicitly names this subgroup. The generating family relation follows Milne, Abelian Varieties, I section 8, with the precise smooth connected parameter convention of def-sfb-line-algebraic-equivalence.
